summary: Gangtok to Lachung is about 120–125 km on the North Sikkim Highway via Kabi, Phodong, Mangan and Chungthang, 6–7 hours on a good day. Tourists travel only in registered local vehicles on a permit, by group package or reserved car. Check current status before you travel.

options.text: The cheapest way. Registered Gangtok operators sell seats in shared Bolero, Xylo or Scorpio vehicles that leave from the North Sikkim stand area around 10 am to noon. The price covers your permit, seat, a basic hotel in Lachung, dinner, breakfast and the Yumthang morning. You share the car with up to nine strangers and follow a fixed schedule.

A private Bolero, Xylo or Innova with a registered local driver, booked through an operator who files your permit. You choose departure time and stops, such as Kabi Lungchok and Phodong. Hotels are extra. Self-drive and plains taxis are not allowed beyond the checkposts.

options.cost: ₹350–500 a seat to Lachung for residents, indicative, 2026
options.text: Local shared jeeps run to Chungthang and Lachung for residents. Tourists cannot use them past the Toong checkpost without a permit issued through an operator. Indian visitors can use shared jeeps as far as Mangan, about ₹250–350, then join their permit vehicle only if the operator agrees in advance.

tip: Ask your driver the evening before to stop at Kabi Lungchok and Phodong, and remember that the Toong checkpost closes to tourist vehicles at 4 pm.

faqs.q: How long does Gangtok to Lachung take
faqs.a: About 6–7 hours for roughly 120–125 km in good conditions, longer during road repairs or after rain. Group vehicles leave Gangtok in the late morning and reach Lachung around dusk. Allow extra time between May and September, when landslides are common.

faqs.q: Can I self-drive from Gangtok to Lachung
faqs.a: No. Tourists must travel in registered local vehicles with local drivers, booked through a registered operator who also files the permit. Plains taxis and self-drive cars are not allowed beyond the checkposts. This rule is enforced at several police and army points.

faqs.q: What is the Toong checkpost time limit
faqs.a: Under the September 2026 order, all tourist and light vehicles going to or returning from Lachung and Lachen must cross the Toong checkpost by 4 pm. This is why groups leave Gangtok by late morning and leave Lachung by midday on the way back. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is the Gangtok–Lachung road open
faqs.a: As of early October 2026, yes; Lachung reopened to tourists in September 2025 after monsoon landslides. Closures are frequent between May and September and after heavy snow in winter. Your operator will know the day's status. Check current status before you travel.

summary: Gangtok to Lachen is about 129 km via Mangan and Chungthang, crossing the new Taram Chu bridge, 6–7 hours. Lachen reopened in 2026 after the 2023 flood; permits come only through registered operators, and the road is fragile. Check current status before you travel.

options.cost: ₹6,000–9,000 per person for Lachen + Lachung 2N/3D, indicative, 2026
options.text: Shared departures for the Lachen–Lachung loop leave Gangtok daily in season. Lachen is usually the first night, so you see Gurudongmar next morning before driving to Lachung. The package includes permit, seat, hotels, most meals and sightseeing. Ask how many people share each vehicle.

options.cost: ₹16,000–22,000 per car for the 2N/3D loop, indicative, 2026
options.text: A private car with a registered local driver lets you add a second night in Lachen to acclimatise, stop where you like and manage timings for older travellers. Hotels are extra. Your operator files the permit, usually several days ahead.

Indian travellers can ride a shared jeep from Gangtok to Mangan without a permit, useful if you want a night at Singhik before going north. From Mangan onward you must be in your operator's permit vehicle; arrange the pickup point with them in advance.

tip: Eat lunch at Chungthang and go to bed early in Lachen; the Gurudongmar day starts at 4 am.

faqs.q: Is the road to Lachen open now
faqs.a: As of early October 2026, yes. Lachen reopened in March 2026 after the Taram Chu bridge was built, closed again from April after road damage, and permits resumed around 10–11 September 2026. Landslides can close it at short notice. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the Taram Chu bridge
faqs.a: It is a new bridge of about 400 feet on the Chungthang–Lachen road, replacing the crossing destroyed after the 2023 flood. Its completion in March 2026 allowed tourist permits for Lachen to resume after 887 days. Rules have required single-vehicle crossing and load limits.

faqs.q: How far is Lachen from Gangtok
faqs.a: About 129 km, roughly 6–7 hours by road through Kabi, Phodong, Mangan and Chungthang. Repairs, single-lane bridges and checkposts can add time. Most groups leave Gangtok in the late morning and reach Lachen around dusk.

faqs.q: Can I go to Lachen and Gurudongmar from Gangtok in one day
faqs.a: No. Lachen is 6–7 hours from Gangtok, and Gurudongmar is a further 3 hours and must be visited early in the morning. You need at least one night in Lachen. A same-day round trip is impossible within checkpost rules and dangerous at 5,430 m.

summary: Lachung to Yumthang is about 24 km up the Lachung valley through the Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary, roughly an hour each way. It is done as a dawn trip in your permit vehicle, returning by late morning.

options.text: Every Lachung package includes the Yumthang morning in the same vehicle that brought you from Gangtok. Cars leave about 5.30–6 am and return by 10–11 am. Ask for short stops in the rhododendron forest in spring.

options.cost: Part of your Lachung car hire
options.text: With a private car you set the departure time and number of stops. For birding or photography, leave at first light and drive slowly through the sanctuary. You cannot hire a separate local taxi for Yumthang unless it is on your permit.

From Yumthang you can continue to Zero Point if the road is open and your permit covers it. Decide at Yumthang after checking the sky and how everyone feels. Pay the driver on the morning, not in advance.

tip: Leave by 6 am; cloud usually fills the valley by late morning.

faqs.q: How far is Yumthang from Lachung
faqs.a: About 24 km, roughly an hour each way through the Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary. Most visitors leave Lachung at 5.30–6 am and are back by 10–11 am. With Zero Point added, allow until about 1 pm.

faqs.q: Is Yumthang included in the Lachung package
faqs.a: Yes, in almost all Lachung packages from Gangtok. Zero Point is usually extra, charged per vehicle. Check your package details for the Yumthang morning and whether breakfast is packed or served on return.

faqs.q: Is the Lachung–Yumthang road open in winter
faqs.a: Usually partly. From December to March snow often stops vehicles short of the valley; drivers go as far as the cleared road allows. After heavy snowfall the trip may be cancelled for a day or two. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I walk from Lachung to Yumthang
faqs.a: Not practically on a tourist permit. The 24 km road climbs about 850 m, and walking it is not part of standard permits. Trekking routes in the area need special permission, registered operators and guides. Use your vehicle and take short walks at stops.

summary: From Yumthang the road climbs above the tree line to Zero Point at Yume Samdong, about 4,660 m, roughly an hour each way. It is an optional add-on paid per vehicle and often closed after mid-December.

options.text: In a shared group vehicle, everyone in the car must agree and share the charge. Decide at Yumthang. If anyone feels unwell or the sky is closed in, skip it. Payment goes to the driver or operator on the morning.

With a private car, you decide with your driver after checking the road status and weather. Leave Lachung by 5.30 am if you plan Zero Point, so you are back in time to cross the Toong checkpost by 4 pm on your way south.

tip: Never prepay Zero Point when booking; pay only on the morning once the road is confirmed open.

faqs.q: How far is Zero Point from Yumthang
faqs.a: Sources give between about 15 and 23 km, and the drive takes roughly an hour each way on a narrow mountain road. Adding Zero Point to the Yumthang morning usually means 2–3 extra hours, plus 20–40 minutes at the top.

faqs.q: When is Zero Point closed
faqs.a: Commonly from about mid-December through the snowiest part of winter, and at any time after heavy snowfall or on official instructions. Spring and autumn are the most reliable. In the monsoon, North Sikkim permits themselves are often suspended. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Zero Point safe for everyone
faqs.a: No. At about 4,660 m it is unsuitable for children under five and for people with heart or lung conditions, and anyone can get altitude sickness. Healthy adults should stay only 20–40 minutes, walk slowly and descend at the first sign of serious symptoms.

faqs.q: Is Zero Point worth the extra money
faqs.a: On a clear day with a healthy, willing group, many people find it worth the ₹3,000–4,500 per vehicle for the snow and height. On a cloudy day, or with vulnerable travellers, it is not. Yumthang alone is a complete morning.

summary: Lachen to Gurudongmar Lake is about 65–70 km via Thangu, roughly 3 hours each way, climbing from about 2,750 m to 5,430 m. Cars leave at 4–5 am. It is the hardest altitude day in Sikkim; children under five should not go.

options.text: Group vehicles leave Lachen at 4–5 am, stop at Thangu for tea and permit checks, reach the lake around 8–10 am and return to Lachen for lunch before driving to Lachung. Everyone in the car must be ready on time.

options.cost: Day's driving part of the loop; ₹6,000–8,000 if hired separately, indicative, 2026
options.text: A private car lets you turn back at Thangu if someone feels unwell without affecting others, and lets you add an acclimatisation night in Lachen. You still leave early, because wind and cloud build after noon.

tip: Agree before leaving Lachen that anyone can ask to turn back, and that Thangu is the place to decide.

faqs.q: What time should I leave Lachen for Gurudongmar
faqs.a: Between 4 and 5 am. The aim is to reach the lake around 8–10 am, when the sky is usually clearest, and start back by noon before the wind and cloud build. Your driver will tell you the exact time the night before.

faqs.q: How long is the Lachen to Gurudongmar drive
faqs.a: About 65–70 km, roughly 3 hours each way, including a tea and permit stop at Thangu. With 20–30 minutes at the lake, the round trip takes 7–9 hours. Most groups then drive on to Lachung after lunch.

faqs.q: Is there oxygen on the way to Gurudongmar
faqs.a: The army runs medical posts on the road where oxygen is available in emergencies. Small oxygen cans are also sold in Gangtok. Oxygen gives relief but is not treatment; descending is. Anyone with serious symptoms should turn back, not continue with a can.

faqs.q: Can foreigners drive from Lachen to Gurudongmar
faqs.a: No. Foreign nationals are not permitted at Gurudongmar Lake. With a Restricted Area Permit they can usually go up the valley as far as Thangu and, where allowed, the Chopta Valley. Mixed groups need separate arrangements. Check current status before you travel.

summary: Lachen to Thangu is about 30 km up the Lachen valley, 1–1.5 hours, climbing from about 2,750 m to roughly 3,900 m. It is the first half of the Gurudongmar drive and the high point for foreign visitors.

options.text: On the Gurudongmar morning, group vehicles reach Thangu around 6 am for tea, toilets and permit checks. For foreign groups, Thangu and Chopta Valley are usually the destination, visited after breakfast rather than at dawn.

options.cost: Part of your Lachen car hire
options.text: With a private car, foreign travellers or anyone not going to Gurudongmar can drive up after breakfast, spend an hour or two at Thangu and Chopta where permitted, and be back in Lachen for lunch.

tip: Use the Thangu halt to check how everyone feels; it is the right place to turn back.

faqs.q: How far is Thangu from Lachen
faqs.a: About 30 km, roughly 1–1.5 hours by road. On the Gurudongmar morning, cars leave Lachen at 4–5 am and reach Thangu around 6 am. Foreign groups and others not going to the lake can drive up after breakfast.

faqs.q: What is the altitude gain from Lachen to Thangu
faqs.a: Lachen is at about 2,750 m and Thangu at roughly 3,900 m, a gain of over 1,100 m in about an hour. Many people feel breathless at Thangu. Move slowly, drink water and watch for headache or nausea.

faqs.q: Is there food at Thangu
faqs.a: Yes. Tea stalls and small canteens sell tea, coffee, noodles, momos, eggs and biscuits, and there are basic toilets. It is the last place with food and toilets before Gurudongmar. Prices are higher than in Gangtok.

faqs.q: Can I stay overnight at Thangu
faqs.a: Basic lodges exist and are sometimes used when permitted, especially for foreign groups. Sleeping at about 3,900 m is cold and raises altitude risk, so we recommend sleeping in Lachen unless you are already well acclimatised.

summary: From Mangan you cross the Teesta into the Lepcha reserve of Dzongu by the Sanklang bridge, rebuilt by the BRO in 2025. Village homestays are 30 minutes to 1.5 hours away. A Dzongu permit is checked at the police post on the far side.

options.text: The easiest way. Your Dzongu homestay sends a car to meet you in the Mangan bazaar, with your permit ready. Distances depend on the village: Passingdang, Lingthem and Hee Gyathang are at different heights and distances on narrow roads.

Local jeeps run between Mangan and Dzongu villages, mainly in the morning and afternoon for residents. You can use them if your permit is ready, but timings are irregular and they fill quickly. Ask your hosts which jeep to take.

If you are coming straight from Gangtok, a reserved car can take you through Mangan into Dzongu. Make sure the driver knows the village and that your permit will be checked at the post after the bridge.

tip: Send ID copies and photographs to your homestay a week ahead so the Dzongu permit is ready when you reach Mangan.

faqs.q: How do I get from Mangan to Dzongu
faqs.a: Cross the Teesta by the Sanklang bridge and continue to your village, usually 30 minutes to 1.5 hours. Most visitors are picked up by their homestay in Mangan for about ₹1,000–2,000, indicative, 2026. Local shared jeeps also run at irregular times.

faqs.q: Where is the Dzongu permit checked
faqs.a: At the police check-post on the Dzongu side, a few kilometres after crossing from the Mangan side. Without a valid permit you will be turned back. Permits are usually arranged in advance by your homestay through the district office in Mangan.

faqs.q: Is the Sanklang bridge open
faqs.a: The Sanklang bridge was rebuilt by the Border Roads Organisation and reopened in 2025, restoring the link into Dzongu. Heavy vehicles have also been routed through Sanklang, Sapho and Shipgyer when the main highway was damaged. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I visit Dzongu as a day trip from Mangan
faqs.a: It is possible with a permit and a car, but it misses the point of Dzongu, which is staying with a Lepcha family. If time is short, one night in a homestay is far better than a day trip. Two or three nights are ideal.

summary: Siliguri (NJP and Bagdogra) to Mangan is about 160–185 km depending on route, 6–7 hours, either via Gangtok or more directly via Rangpo, Singtam and Dikchu. It is the plains gateway for Dzongu, Singhik and the North Sikkim Highway.

options.text: Take a shared jeep from Siliguri to Gangtok, ₹350–500 a seat, then another from Gangtok's North Sikkim stand to Mangan, ₹250–350. It is cheap but long, and the Mangan jeeps leave mainly in the morning, so you may need a night in Gangtok.

options.mode: Reserved car via Singtam and Dikchu
options.text: A reserved car can skip Gangtok and take the shorter route via Sevoke, Rangpo, Singtam and Dikchu straight to Mangan. Good for groups heading directly to Dzongu or Singhik. Indians need no permit as far as Mangan.

Some shared jeeps run from Siliguri directly to Mangan on certain days, mainly in the morning. Ask at the Sikkim jeep stands near Siliguri's SNT or Pradhan Nagar. Availability changes; do not rely on it for a tight plan.

tip: Start from Siliguri by 8 am so you reach Mangan or Dzongu before dark.

faqs.q: How far is Mangan from Siliguri
faqs.a: About 160–185 km depending on the route, roughly 6–7 hours. The direct route goes via Sevoke, Rangpo, Singtam and Dikchu; the alternative goes through Gangtok and then north on the North Sikkim Highway. Road works along the Teesta can add time.

faqs.q: Is there a direct bus or jeep from Siliguri to Mangan
faqs.a: Some shared jeeps run directly on certain days, mainly in the morning, for about ₹450–650 a seat, indicative, 2026. Otherwise change at Gangtok. Sikkim state buses have run on some routes but are infrequent. Ask at the Siliguri jeep stands the day before.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit from Siliguri to Mangan
faqs.a: Indian citizens need no permit to travel from Siliguri to Mangan. Foreign nationals need the standard Sikkim permit, issued at entry or online. Beyond Mangan, the Toong checkpost requires a North Sikkim permit, and Dzongu needs its own permit.

faqs.q: Should I go to Mangan via Gangtok or directly
faqs.a: If you are heading straight to Dzongu or Singhik, the direct route via Singtam and Dikchu saves time. If you need to collect permits, change money or want a night in the capital, go via Gangtok. Shared-jeep travellers usually go via Gangtok because of connections.
